$comment: Pin id -> the repository paths that CONSUME that COMMIT-BEARING design pin (cinatra#3144). One map, shared by the three gates that read the pin: design-pin-freshness (is the pin still current), design-anchor-resolution (do the anchors it records resolve in the drawings it governs) and design-record-grammar (does a graded record name the pin it was graded against). The rule is design-pin-drift's, reused rather than reinvented: on a pull_request / merge_group / a push to any other branch a gate is red only for the pins whose mapped paths this diff touched, so an unrelated pull request is never blocked by a lag it does not adopt; on a push to main and on dispatch, any finding is red. Three classes of path per pin, and no others: the two files that CARRY the pin, the engines that read it (the digest engine, the capture-requirement recorder, the acceptance gate that refuses a stale digest), and the executable expectations bound to it. globalPaths change what the gates themselves decide, so touching one of them touches every id — after such a change no pin's silence is trustworthy. Every path here must exist: the gates' suites refuse a mapped path that is gone.
